item.title: Trump announces new tariffs, investigations after Supreme Court ruling
item.description: President Trump said Friday he would raise preexisting tariffs and begin the process of imposing new ones after the Supreme Court struck down many of his import taxes on foreign trading partners.

item.description: Scott Charter School may close at the end of the 2026-2027 school year.

item.title: Little Rock Air Force Base conducts prescribed burn to prevent wildfires
item.description: The Little Rock Air Force Base had started conducting prescribed burns to create burn layers, preventing future wildfires from spreading onto the base. Randy Cozad with Barksdale Air Force Wildlife Fire Support Module explained what a burn layer was.

item.title: Little Rock ad agency designs U.S.A. Curling team logo for 2026 Winter Olympics
item.description: If you've been tuned in to the United States Curling team in action at the Winter Olympics, you've already seen the logo countless times, but what you might not know is that it was designed by a long-standing advertising agency based in the heart of Arkansas' capital city.

item.title: Olympic buzz draws skaters to Arkansas Skatium
item.description: As international competition shines a spotlight on winter sports, more Arkansans are heading to the rink to try skating for themselves.

item.title: Little Rock small business owner expects to feel ripple effects of back and forth on tariffs
item.description: A U.S. Supreme Court decision striking down many of President Donald Trump’s sweeping global tariffs is creating fresh uncertainty for small businesses in Arkansas, including one Little Rock pottery studio that relies on imported materials.

item.title: Early voting underway in Arkansas for the March 3 primary & election
item.description: Arkansans can early vote from Feb. 17 through March 2 for the March 3 election, which includes a preferential primary and a special election for House District 70 and Senate District 26.

item.title: Arkansas State Police seize more than 775 pounds of drugs in four traffic stops
item.description: Arkansas State Police seized over 775 pounds of illegal narcotics in a series of traffic stops, resulting in the arrest of four individuals facing felony charges.
